newsitem.title: UK: Wet Brent holds steady in otherwise weak North Sea.
newsitem.headline: Wet Brent holds steady in otherwise weak North Sea.

text.p: Dated Brent paused for breath on Thursday, steadying after a two-week slide in which the benchmark grade has shed over 60 cents.
But other grades weakened with availabilities plentiful, traders said.
A Brent loading June 12-14 changed hands at July Brent -48 cents, the same price that a 10-12 loader fetched on Wednesday.
The lone Brent date, loading June 20-22, was kept ahead of the five o'clock deadline by Stasco.
A cross-month Forties traded at Dated Brent +18 cents, seven cents down on the last deal done, while a Draugen loading June 16-18 also traded weaker at Dated Brent +18 cents.
"(Refining) margins aren't as good as they have been, and avails are good. The grades are going to be weaker," said one trader.
A closed transatlantic arbitrage meant that supply pressure was building up within the region.
"The water level is rising but there's no outlet for it," one dealer said.
The Brent cash market was also easier with the June/July intermonth spread traded at -33 cents, and July/August at a low of -23 cents, five cents down on Wednesday's levels.
CFDs also sank about five cents lower with next week's dates (June 9-13) talked at July Brent -50/-47 late in the day.
Outright prices fell with July Brent trading 27 cents down at $18.45 a barrel on the IPE screen at 1725 GMT.
The West African market was pressured by several unsold June cargoes, which added up to some 15 million barrels, traders said.
The overhang was stifling marketing efforts for July barrels, they said.

"The market seems quite bearish, there's plenty of North African and some North Sea (grades) and I don't know what is going to happen to the July (West African) barrels with still a lot of June around," one trader said.
Traders said that FOB buyers had all but disappeared, and sellers would have to offload barrels into the U.S. on a delivered basis.
A trading house holding a third decade Brass River was heard to have sold some of the cargo into the U.S.
June Bonny Light was being assessed in the Dated Brent plus mid forties while Forcados around the 20 mark.
But traders said pressure has partially lifted off Qua Iboe after a seller was reported to have found a home for part of a VLCC of the Nigerian grade.
There was unconfirmed talk of a Swiss-based trader selling a second decade July of Oso condensate recently but no further details were available.
A June 22-24 Escravos was heard sold at Dated Brent +32 cents earlier in the week.
--Rosalind Russell, Haitham Haddadin, London +44171 542 5387
